kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY VOLCANO ACTIVITY NOTIFICATION
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - Precursory low-level eruptive activity before episode 57 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption began around 1:21 a.m. HST on November 22, 2026.
kilauea_notices.detail: Precursory low-level activity for episode 57 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption at the summit of Kīlauea began around 1:21 a.m. HST on November 22 with precursory overflows from the north vent. There have been 2 additional overflows with the last ending at 3:03 a.m. HST. The overflows lasted 15-20 minutes each. Both the north and southwest vents continue to emit strong glow with frequent visible spatter and flames between eruptions of precursory overflows. Intermittent overflows are expected to continue until the onset of episode 57 fountains. Accordingly, HVO is raising the Alert Level for Kīlauea from ADVISORY to WATCH and the Aviation Color Code from YELLOW to ORANGE. Alert level and aviation color code definitions: https://www.usgs.gov/programs/VHP/alert-level-system. This low-level precursory activity can continue for hours to days before the lava fountaining episode beings. The forecast for episode 57 of lava fountaining to start is between Sunday November 22 and Thursday November 26. Another VAN will be published when lava fountaining episode 57 fountaining begins. Ground level winds are currently from the north northeast at 10-15 mph blowing the volcanic gas plume to the south southwest. No tephra is being produced at this time. All eruptive vents and lava flows are confined to Halemaʻumaʻu crater within Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. Tephra fall from volcanic ash clouds is greatest within 3 miles (5 km) of the vents, lighter ash and Pele's Hair may stay suspended for large distances from the vents. Support science and community awareness by reporting tephra fall: https://hawaiiash.science/report_form Three Kīlauea summit livestream videos that show eruptive lava fountains are available here: https://youtube.com/@usgs/streams KPcam and MKcam provide views of the plume height for aviation purposes Additional short updates as the episode progresses will be posted here: https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/hvo/observatory-messages Timeline of eruptive episodes since December 23, 2024: https://www.usgs.gov/volcanoes/kilauea/science/eruption-information Most lava fountaining episodes since December 23, 2024, have continued for a day or less.

mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
